item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the New York Times Editing Residency 2027–2029, a paid, full-time programme designed to develop the next generation of newsroom editors.

The two-year residency combines practical editing experience, structured professional training and rotations across different desks within The New York Times newsroom. Residents will work alongside experienced journalists and editors while strengthening the judgment, clarity, precision and contextual awareness required to shape high-quality journalism.

The New York Times plans to select three editing residents, who are expected to join the organisation in late January 2027. Successful applicants will work full time, receive employee benefits and participate in dedicated training and speaker programmes throughout the residency.

The most competitive candidates will have between two and seven years of professional journalism experience, together with a clear commitment to developing the craft of editing.

Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, 8 September 2026.

About the New York Times Editing Residency

The New York Times Editing Residency is an early-career professional development programme created to cultivate editors who can help shape the future of journalism.

Editing remains one of the most important functions within a newsroom. Editors do far more than correct spelling, grammar or punctuation. They help determine whether a story is accurate, clear, fair, well-structured and appropriately presented for its intended audience.

Strong editors must be able to:

  • Exercise sound editorial judgment
  • Identify gaps in reporting
  • Improve clarity and organisation
  • Evaluate context and accuracy
  • Work collaboratively with reporters
  • Protect the integrity of published journalism
  • Adapt stories for different formats and audiences
  • Recognise ethical, legal and reputational concerns

The residency reflects the reality that editing continues to change as news organisations increasingly use visual journalism, multimedia storytelling, data, graphics, video, interactive formats and other digital approaches.

Residents will therefore enter a newsroom environment in which editing is both a traditional journalistic discipline and an evolving creative practice.

Purpose of the Programme

The central purpose of the residency is to provide promising journalists with the practical experience, guidance and professional tools needed to become accomplished editors.

The programme seeks to develop candidates who can contribute meaningfully to journalism while learning from editors across The New York Times.

Its objectives include:

  • Developing the next generation of newsroom editors
  • Strengthening editorial judgment and decision-making
  • Providing practical experience across different newsroom desks
  • Building confidence in editing complex stories
  • Exposing residents to different forms of journalism
  • Supporting professional growth through structured training
  • Creating pathways for candidates from diverse backgrounds
  • Helping residents understand how a major international newsroom operates

Rather than placing participants in one narrow role for the entire programme, the residency provides exposure to multiple areas of the newsroom.

Residency Duration

The New York Times Editing Residency is a two-year, full-time programme covering the 2027–2029 period.

The three selected residents are expected to begin working at The Times in late January 2027.

Because this is a full-time professional commitment, applicants should be prepared to participate throughout the entire residency period and carry out the responsibilities associated with their assigned newsroom desks.

Desk Rotations

Residents will work across a range of desks during the programme.

The information provided does not identify the exact desks or specify how long each rotation will last. However, the rotational structure is intended to expose participants to different editorial environments, workflows, subject areas and forms of storytelling.

A desk rotation may help residents understand how editorial priorities vary depending on:

  • The type of journalism being produced
  • The subject matter being covered
  • The intended audience
  • The speed of the news cycle
  • The format of the final publication
  • The level of collaboration required
  • The reporting and production resources available

Working across multiple desks can also help residents identify their editorial strengths and determine which areas of journalism they may wish to pursue in the future.

What Editing Residents Will Gain

Practical Newsroom Experience

Residents will work inside The New York Times newsroom and contribute to the editorial process on a full-time basis.

This practical experience is central to the programme. Participants will not simply observe newsroom operations; they will gain direct exposure to the decisions, responsibilities and collaborative relationships that shape published journalism.

Development of Editorial Judgment

Editorial judgment involves deciding what information matters, what requires further reporting, what may confuse readers and how a story should be framed or organised.

Residents will have opportunities to strengthen their ability to assess:

  • Accuracy
  • Relevance
  • Structure
  • Tone
  • Clarity
  • Context
  • Fairness
  • Reader understanding

These skills are difficult to acquire through theory alone. They require repeated practice, feedback and guidance from experienced professionals.

Dedicated Training

Residents will participate in training programmes created specifically to support their professional development.

The announcement does not provide a complete curriculum, but the training is expected to complement residents’ practical work across the newsroom.

Training may help participants reflect on their editorial decisions, understand newsroom standards and develop skills that can be applied throughout their careers.

Speaker Programmes

Editing residents will also attend dedicated speaker programmes at The New York Times.

These sessions may provide opportunities to hear from experienced journalists, editors and newsroom leaders about their work, professional development and perspectives on the changing media industry.

Exposure to Evolving Storytelling Formats

Modern journalism is increasingly produced through combinations of text, images, graphics, video, audio, data and interactive formats.

The residency offers participants an opportunity to understand how editing operates within this broader storytelling environment.

Editors must increasingly consider not only the words in an article but also how different elements work together to communicate information clearly and responsibly.

Professional Network Development

Working across desks will allow residents to build relationships with journalists, editors and newsroom leaders.

These professional connections may become an important source of mentorship, collaboration and career guidance during and after the programme.

Compensation and Benefits

The New York Times Editing Residency is a paid programme.

Residents will:

  • Work full time
  • Receive compensation
  • Receive employee benefits
  • Participate in dedicated training
  • Attend speaker programmes
  • Gain experience across multiple newsroom desks

The available information does not state the exact salary, financial package or individual benefits. Applicants should consult the official application page for complete employment terms.

Number of Available Positions

The New York Times plans to welcome:

Three editing residents

Because only three participants are expected to be selected, the application process is likely to be highly competitive.

Candidates should ensure that their applications clearly demonstrate both relevant journalism experience and a genuine commitment to editing.

Who Should Apply?

The programme is intended for early-career and developing journalists who want to strengthen their editorial skills.

The most competitive applicants will have:

  • At least two years of professional journalism experience
  • No more than seven years of professional journalism experience
  • A demonstrated commitment to editing
  • Some newsroom editing experience
  • Strong editorial judgment
  • An interest in learning across multiple desks
  • The ability to work collaboratively
  • A commitment to clear and responsible journalism

The announcement indicates that candidates with existing newsroom editing experience are likely to be particularly competitive.

However, applicants should not view editing only as a formal job title. Journalists may have gained relevant experience by editing colleagues’ work, managing publications, coordinating reporting projects, reviewing scripts or shaping stories for digital and multimedia platforms.

Professional Experience Requirement

The preferred experience range is:

A minimum of two years and a maximum of seven years of professional journalism experience

This range suggests that the programme is aimed at journalists who have already gained meaningful professional experience but remain at a relatively early stage in their careers.

Applicants with fewer than two years or more than seven years of experience may be less competitive based on the stated criteria.

The announcement refers specifically to professional journalism experience. Candidates should therefore clearly document the nature, duration and responsibilities of their journalism work.

Commitment to the Craft of Editing

A strong application should communicate why the candidate wants to become an editor and how their previous experience has prepared them for the residency.

Commitment to editing may be demonstrated through experience such as:

  • Editing reported articles
  • Working on a student or professional publication
  • Providing structural feedback to writers
  • Fact-checking
  • Managing editorial workflows
  • Editing newsletters or digital content
  • Coordinating collaborative reporting
  • Reviewing multimedia scripts
  • Supporting publication standards
  • Working with reporters to strengthen stories

Candidates should focus on meaningful examples rather than simply stating that they enjoy writing or journalism.

Diversity and Inclusion

The New York Times states that it aims to recruit candidates from diverse backgrounds.

The goal is to provide participants with the tools and experiences they need to help shape journalism.

Diversity may contribute to stronger journalism by expanding the perspectives, experiences and forms of knowledge represented in editorial decision-making.

No racial, ethnic, gender or national group is identified as an exclusive eligibility category in the information provided.

Selection Process

Applications will close on 8 September 2026.

After the deadline, the programme directors and editors from across the newsroom will work together to select the residents.

The process is expected to assess:

  • Professional journalism experience
  • Editing experience
  • Commitment to editorial work
  • Career potential
  • Ability to contribute to the newsroom
  • Alignment with the programme’s development goals

Only three residents are expected to be appointed.

The available information does not explain whether shortlisted candidates will complete interviews, assessments or editing exercises. Applicants should therefore review the official application instructions carefully.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit their applications through the official application page.

Applicants should follow the instructions on the application platform and provide all requested information and supporting materials.

Questions about the programme may be directed to the relevant Early Career Programs team contact identified in the official announcement.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, 8 September 2026

Late applications may not be considered.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours before the deadline, as last-minute technical problems, incomplete uploads or missing information can turn a promising application into a small digital tragedy.

Why Apply for the New York Times Editing Residency?

The residency offers an unusual combination of professional employment and structured editorial development.

Participants will receive:

  • Two years of full-time newsroom experience
  • Paid employment and benefits
  • Rotations across different desks
  • Dedicated editorial training
  • Access to speaker programmes
  • Guidance from experienced editors
  • Exposure to different forms of storytelling
  • Opportunities to build a professional network
  • A chance to contribute to an internationally recognised news organisation

For journalists committed to editing, the programme provides an opportunity to deepen their craft while learning how editorial decisions are made in a complex, fast-moving newsroom.

Conclusion

The New York Times Editing Residency 2027–2029 is a paid, two-year opportunity for developing journalists who want to become stronger editors.

Three residents will work full time across multiple newsroom desks, receive benefits and participate in dedicated training and speaker programmes. The residency is designed to strengthen editorial judgment, clarity, contextual understanding and the ability to shape journalism across traditional and evolving storytelling formats.

The most competitive candidates will have between two and seven years of professional journalism experience and will demonstrate a clear commitment to editing.

Applications close at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on 8 September 2026, and the selected residents are expected to begin working at The New York Times in late January 2027.

For further information about this opportunity, CLICK HERE.

To discover more job opportunities, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) has officially launched its 2026 Calls for Proposals, offering substantial funding opportunities for European Union Member States to implement strategic migration initiatives with partner countries. Backed by the European Union, the latest funding calls are designed to strengthen international cooperation on migration management, border governance, and internal security while promoting sustainable partnerships between EU Member States and partner nations.

With a combined financial envelope of €14 million, the 2026 Calls for Proposals are open on a rolling basis, allowing eligible applicants to submit proposals until all available funds have been allocated. This flexible application model provides applicants with the opportunity to prepare strong project proposals while encouraging early submissions due to limited available funding.

If your institution is involved in migration governance, border management, or international cooperation, this funding opportunity could support impactful projects that contribute to the implementation of the European Union Migration Policy’s External Dimension.

About the Migration Partnership Facility (MPF)

The Migration Partnership Facility (MPF) is an initiative that supports the implementation of migration partnerships between European Union Member States and partner countries. The facility translates strategic priorities under the EU Migration Policy’s External Dimension into practical projects through competitive grant funding.

The programme enables eligible institutions to develop and implement migration-related initiatives that address shared migration challenges while fostering stronger international cooperation.

Through its grant programme, the MPF finances projects that contribute to:

  • Better migration governance
  • Stronger partnerships between the EU and partner countries
  • Improved border management systems
  • Enhanced internal security cooperation
  • Capacity development
  • Sustainable migration solutions
  • Knowledge sharing and institutional collaboration

The Migration Partnership Facility serves as an important mechanism for transforming migration policy priorities into practical actions that generate measurable impact.

2026 Migration Partnership Facility Calls for Proposals

The 2026 funding round includes three separate funding windows, each targeting a different strategic priority.

1. Call for Proposals 2026 – Migration Partnerships

The Migration Partnerships Call aims to strengthen cooperation between EU Member States and partner countries through projects that improve migration governance and partnership implementation.

Funding Available

  • Financial envelope: €6,000,000
  • Funding Source: Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF)

Opening Date

  • 13 July 2026

Deadline

There is no fixed application deadline.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the available funding has been fully committed.

Because funding is limited, applicants are encouraged to submit proposals as early as possible.

2. Call for Proposals 2026 – Border Management

The Border Management Call focuses on strengthening border governance, improving migration management systems, and supporting projects that contribute to effective border administration.

Funding Available

  • Financial envelope: €5,000,000
  • Funding Source: Border Management and Visa Instrument (BMVI)

Opening Date

  • 13 July 2026

Deadline

There is no closing date.

Applications remain open on a rolling basis until the available funding has been exhausted.

Early application is strongly recommended.

3. Call for Proposals 2026 – Internal Security

The Internal Security Call supports initiatives that enhance cooperation in internal security while contributing to broader migration management objectives.

Funding Available

  • Financial envelope: €3,000,000
  • Funding Source:
    • Internal Security Fund (ISF)

Opening Date

  • 13 July 2026

Deadline

No fixed deadline has been established.

Applications will continue to be reviewed and funded until the allocated budget has been fully utilized.

Total Funding Available

Across all three calls, the Migration Partnership Facility has allocated:

Funding Window Financial Envelope
Migration Partnerships €6,000,000
Border Management €5,000,000
Internal Security €3,000,000

Total Available Funding: €14,000,000

Objectives of the 2026 Calls

The funding programme aims to support projects that contribute to implementing the European Union’s external migration priorities by:

  • Strengthening migration partnerships
  • Promoting cooperation between EU Member States and partner countries
  • Enhancing migration governance
  • Supporting border management reforms
  • Improving institutional capacities
  • Advancing internal security cooperation
  • Facilitating sustainable migration solutions
  • Encouraging collaborative project implementation

These objectives help ensure that migration is managed in a coordinated, secure, and mutually beneficial manner.

Why This Funding Opportunity Matters

Migration remains one of the European Union’s major policy priorities. Effective migration governance requires close cooperation between countries of origin, transit, and destination.

The Migration Partnership Facility provides practical financial support that enables governments and eligible institutions to transform strategic migration priorities into operational programmes.

Through these grants, successful applicants can:

  • Develop innovative migration management initiatives
  • Strengthen institutional partnerships
  • Improve border management systems
  • Build technical and operational capacities
  • Enhance regional cooperation
  • Promote sustainable migration governance
  • Support policy implementation
  • Deliver measurable development outcomes

Rolling Application Process

Unlike many grant programmes that operate with a fixed deadline, the Migration Partnership Facility accepts applications on a continuous basis.

This means:

  • Applications can be submitted at any time.
  • Proposals are reviewed as they are received.
  • Funding is awarded while resources remain available.
  • Once the allocated budget has been exhausted, the calls will close.

Applicants are therefore encouraged to prepare and submit proposals early to maximize their chances of securing funding.

Funding Sources

The 2026 Calls are financed through three major European Union funding instruments:

Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF)

Supports initiatives that improve migration management, integration, asylum systems, and international migration partnerships.

Border Management and Visa Instrument (BMVI)

Supports projects aimed at strengthening border management systems, visa policies, and external border cooperation.

Internal Security Fund (ISF)

Finances initiatives that enhance security cooperation, institutional resilience, and internal security capacities.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants should prepare project proposals that align with the objectives of the respective funding window.

Applicants should:

  1. Review the relevant Call for Proposals.
  2. Ensure that their proposed project aligns with the funding priorities.
  3. Prepare all required documentation.
  4. Submit the proposal while funding remains available.

For support or general enquiries regarding the Calls for Proposals, applicants may contact the Migration Partnership Facility via:

Email: mpf@icmpd.org

APPLY HERE

Important Dates

  • Call Opening Date: 13 July 2026
  • Application Deadline: No fixed deadline. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until funds are fully allocated.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Migration Partnership Facility 2026 Calls for Proposals.

Key Highlights

  • Up to €14 million available across three funding calls.
  • Rolling applications with no fixed deadline.
  • Three specialized funding windows.
  • Supports implementation of the EU Migration Policy’s External Dimension.
  • Encourages cooperation between EU Member States and partner countries.
  • Focus areas include migration partnerships, border management, and internal security.
  • Projects are financed through AMIF, BMVI, and ISF.
  • Early submission is encouraged due to limited funding.

Conclusion

The Migration Partnership Facility 2026 Calls for Proposals present a significant opportunity for eligible EU Member States to secure funding for projects that strengthen international migration cooperation, border governance, and internal security. With a total funding envelope of €14 million and a rolling application process, institutions have the flexibility to develop high-quality proposals while responding to evolving migration priorities. However, since funding will be awarded until available resources are exhausted, prospective applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their proposals as early as possible. Organizations capable of delivering impactful migration-related initiatives should take advantage of this opportunity to contribute to stronger international partnerships and more effective migration governance.

For more grant opportunities visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Introduction

The UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association is pleased to announce the opening of applications for the 2026/27 Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship, a prestigious opportunity designed to strengthen the advocacy strand of the Association’s activities and advance the theme of Openness and Transparency within the Digital Humanities community. This fellowship represents a significant investment in the future of Digital Humanities across the UK and Ireland, offering researchers, practitioners, and professionals the chance to contribute meaningfully to the evolving landscape of institutional and policy drivers that shape the discipline.

Digital Humanities, as an interdisciplinary field, continues to expand its influence across academic institutions, cultural heritage organizations, and policy-making bodies. The need for effective advocacy has never been greater. As universities, libraries, archives, museums, and funding bodies grapple with questions of openness, transparency, and equitable access to knowledge, the role of advocacy becomes central to ensuring that Digital Humanities remains responsive, inclusive, and impactful. The Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship is designed to address this need by appointing a dedicated fellow who will undertake research, stakeholder engagement, and community-building activities over a twelve-month period.

This fellowship is not merely an appointment; it is a call to action. It invites individuals with a passion for Digital Humanities to step forward and help shape the discourse around openness and transparency. By engaging with stakeholders across sectors, developing value propositions, and contributing to best practice guidance, the fellow will play a pivotal role in ensuring that the Association’s advocacy efforts align with the evolving needs of the community. The fellowship also provides a platform for underrepresented voices, encouraging diversity and inclusivity in Digital Humanities advocacy.

The 2026/27 Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship is structured to provide flexibility, support, and recognition. With a remuneration package of £4,000, supplemented by £1,000 for fellowship-related activities, the fellow will be empowered to dedicate approximately ten hours per month to this work. The fellowship is designed to accommodate varying professional circumstances, allowing for adjustments in start and completion dates, and offering the possibility of joint applications for those who wish to share the role.

Applications are invited from individuals resident in the UK or Ireland, with experience in research, digital practice, technical innovation, or cultural heritage. The Association particularly welcomes applications from those traditionally underrepresented in Digital Humanities, recognizing the importance of diverse perspectives in shaping advocacy strategies. The fellowship will commence in October 2026, following a rigorous selection process that includes shortlisting in late August and interviews in early September.

This article provides a comprehensive overview of the fellowship, including its objectives, responsibilities, funding arrangements, application process, and expected outputs. It also explores the broader significance of advocacy in Digital Humanities, the theme of openness and transparency, and the potential impact of the fellowship on the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities community. A detailed FAQ section is included to address common queries, ensuring that prospective applicants have access to all the information they need to prepare a strong application.

Section 1: Fellowship Overview

The Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship is a cornerstone initiative of the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association. It is designed to advance the Association’s mission of fostering collaboration, innovation, and advocacy within the Digital Humanities community. The fellowship provides a structured yet flexible framework for individuals to contribute to the Association’s advocacy plan, focusing on the theme of Openness and Transparency for the 2026/27 cycle.

Key Features of the Fellowship:

  1. Duration and Commitment
    • Twelve months, commencing in October 2026.
    • Approximately ten hours per month dedicated to fellowship activities.
    • Flexibility in scheduling, with options for late start or early completion.
  2. Remuneration and Support
    • £4,000 stipend, paid in three instalments.
    • £1,000 additional support for fellowship-related expenses (travel, events, catering, etc.).
    • Potential access to additional funds for attending key Digital Humanities events.
  3. Eligibility
    • Applicants must be resident in the UK or Ireland.
    • Open to researchers, digital practitioners, technical professionals, and GLAM sector professionals.
    • Applications encouraged from underrepresented groups in Digital Humanities.
    • Joint applications accepted for job-sharing arrangements.
  4. Responsibilities
    • Undertake research into Digital Humanities in the UK and Ireland.
    • Engage with stakeholders through surveys, interviews, focus groups, and workshops.
    • Develop value propositions to support advocacy efforts.
    • Contribute to community engagement around openness and transparency.
    • Produce outputs such as reports, podcasts, videos, or other media, shared openly with the community.
  5. Theme: Openness and Transparency
    • Projects should explore advocacy in relation to openness and transparency.
    • Potential areas include cross-sector collaboration, policy-level advocacy, improving access to digital scholarship, and developing best practice guidance.

Section 2: Theme – Openness and Transparency

The 2026/27 Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship is anchored in the theme of Openness and Transparency, a principle that lies at the very heart of contemporary Digital Humanities. This theme is not incidental; it reflects a deliberate choice by the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association to foreground values that are increasingly critical in academic, cultural, and policy contexts. By focusing on openness and transparency, the fellowship seeks to address pressing challenges in research culture, knowledge dissemination, and cross-sector collaboration, while also promoting inclusivity and accountability.

2.1 The Significance of Openness in Digital Humanities

Openness in Digital Humanities encompasses a wide range of practices and commitments, including:

  • Open Access to Scholarship: Ensuring that research outputs are freely available to the public, thereby democratizing access to knowledge and reducing barriers for researchers, practitioners, and communities outside traditional academic institutions.
  • Open Data and Resources: Promoting the sharing of datasets, tools, and methodologies to enable replication, innovation, and collaborative research across disciplines and sectors.
  • Open Collaboration: Encouraging partnerships between higher education institutions, cultural heritage organizations, technical professionals, and community groups to foster diverse perspectives and shared ownership of Digital Humanities projects.
  • Open Pedagogy: Developing teaching and training resources that are accessible to a wide audience, thereby expanding the reach of Digital Humanities education and capacity-building.

Openness is not merely a technical or logistical matter; it is a philosophical commitment to inclusivity, equity, and the democratization of knowledge. By embedding openness into advocacy strategies, the fellowship aims to ensure that Digital Humanities remains a field that is accessible, responsive, and relevant to a broad spectrum of stakeholders.

2.2 Transparency as a Core Value

Transparency complements openness by emphasizing clarity, accountability, and integrity in research and advocacy practices. Within the context of Digital Humanities, transparency involves:

  • Transparent Research Practices: Clearly articulating methodologies, assumptions, and limitations in research outputs to foster trust and credibility.
  • Transparent Policy Engagement: Ensuring that advocacy efforts with funders, national bodies, and institutions are conducted openly, with clear communication of objectives, processes, and outcomes.
  • Transparent Community Engagement: Building trust with stakeholders by maintaining open lines of communication, sharing progress and challenges, and inviting feedback throughout the fellowship.
  • Transparent Evaluation and Reporting: Producing outputs that are not only accessible but also accompanied by documentation that explains how conclusions were reached and how recommendations can be implemented.

Transparency is essential for building legitimacy in advocacy efforts. It reassures stakeholders that Digital Humanities is a field committed to ethical practices, rigorous standards, and accountability to the communities it serves.

2.3 The Fellowship’s Role in Advancing Openness and Transparency

The Advocacy & Engagement Fellow will play a pivotal role in operationalizing the theme of openness and transparency. This will involve:

  1. Mapping Practices Across the UK and Ireland
    • Conducting desk research to identify existing practices of openness and transparency in Digital Humanities.
    • Surveying the community to gather insights into challenges, opportunities, and best practices.
    • Contextualizing differences between Ireland and the UK, particularly in relation to frameworks such as REF, UKRI, Research Ireland, and Impact 2030.
  2. Engaging Stakeholders
    • Organizing interviews, focus groups, and workshops to facilitate dialogue around openness and transparency.
    • Building cross-sector partnerships with non-HEI organizations and communities to expand the reach of Digital Humanities advocacy.
  3. Developing Value Propositions
    • Creating clear, evidence-based arguments that demonstrate the value of openness and transparency in Digital Humanities.
    • Providing researchers with tools to articulate the significance of their work in policy and funding contexts.
  4. Producing Outputs
    • Generating reports, podcasts, videos, or other media that document findings and recommendations.
    • Ensuring that all outputs are shared openly with the Digital Humanities community, thereby embodying the principles of openness and transparency.

2.4 Potential Areas of Exploration

The fellowship invites projects that explore openness and transparency in diverse ways. Potential areas include:

  • Cross-Sector Collaboration: Developing best practice guidance, collaborative tools, or training programs to support partnerships between academia and non-HEI organizations.
  • Research Culture Improvement: Investigating how openness and transparency can enhance research culture, particularly by addressing differences in practices between Ireland and the UK.
  • Public Access to Scholarship: Identifying barriers to open access and proposing strategies to improve public engagement with digital scholarship.
  • Policy-Level Advocacy: Crafting value propositions that highlight the importance of Digital Humanities in policy and funding contexts, thereby strengthening the field’s position in national and institutional agendas.

2.5 Broader Impact of the Theme

By centering the fellowship on openness and transparency, the UK-Ireland Digital Humanities Association is making a strategic statement about the future of the field. The fellowship is not only about individual outputs; it is about shaping a culture of advocacy that prioritizes inclusivity, accountability, and accessibility. The impact of this theme will extend beyond the fellowship year, influencing how Digital Humanities is practiced, taught, and valued across the UK and Ireland.

Section 3: Eligibility and Qualifications

The 2026/27 Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship is open to a wide range of applicants, reflecting the interdisciplinary and cross-sector nature of Digital Humanities. The Association recognizes that advocacy requires diverse perspectives, and therefore encourages applications from individuals across different professional and academic backgrounds.

3.1 Residency Requirement

  • Applicants must be resident in the United Kingdom or Ireland.
  • This requirement ensures that fellows are embedded within the regional context of the Association’s work, enabling them to engage directly with stakeholders and communities in both countries.

3.2 Professional Backgrounds

Applications are welcomed from individuals with experience in:

  • Academic Research: Scholars conducting research in Digital Humanities or related fields.
  • Digital Practitioners: Professionals engaged in digital projects, tool development, or digital scholarship.
  • Technical Professionals: Individuals with expertise in computing, data management, or technical infrastructure relevant to Digital Humanities.
  • GLAM Sector Professionals: Staff from galleries, libraries, archives, and museums who are interested in expanding their role within the Digital Humanities community.

3.3 Diversity and Inclusion

  • The Association particularly encourages applications from those traditionally underrepresented in Digital Humanities.
  • Diversity is seen as a strength, and the fellowship aims to amplify voices that have historically been marginalized in academic and cultural contexts.

3.4 Joint Applications

  • The fellowship allows for job-sharing arrangements, enabling two individuals to apply jointly.
  • Joint applicants must submit a single application form and statement of interest, but provide individual CVs and letters of support.

3.5 Letters of Support

  • Applicants who are currently enrolled as students or employed by an organization must provide a letter of support from their manager or academic supervisor.
  • This letter should acknowledge that approximately ten hours per month will be dedicated to fellowship activities.

Section 4: Fellowship Responsibilities and Outputs

The Advocacy & Engagement Fellow will undertake a range of responsibilities designed to advance the Association’s advocacy plan. These responsibilities are structured to ensure that the fellowship produces tangible outputs while also fostering community engagement.

4.1 Research Activities

  • Desk Research: Reviewing existing literature, policies, and practices related to openness and transparency in Digital Humanities.
  • Community Surveys: Designing and administering surveys to gather insights from the Digital Humanities community.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Conducting interviews, focus groups, and workshops with key stakeholders.

4.2 Value Proposition Development

  • Based on research and engagement activities, the fellow will develop a set of value propositions that articulate the significance of Digital Humanities in policy and funding contexts.
  • These propositions will serve as tools for researchers and practitioners to advocate for their work.

4.3 Community Engagement

  • The fellow will contribute to wider community engagement around advocacy, openness, and transparency.
  • This may include organizing sessions at in-person events, contributing to regional meetings, and producing accessible outputs.

4.4 Outputs

The fellowship requires the production of outputs that are shared openly with the community. These may include:

  • Written reports.
  • Podcasts.
  • Videos.
  • Other media forms.

All outputs must be accompanied by supporting documentation and a proposed implementation plan.

Section 5: Value, Duration, and Funding

5.1 Duration

  • The fellowship will last for 12 months, commencing in October 2026.
  • Exact start and completion dates can be adjusted to accommodate the fellow’s circumstances.

5.2 Time Commitment

  • Approximately 10 hours per month.
  • Flexible scheduling to allow fellows to balance other professional or academic commitments.

5.3 Remuneration

  • £4,000 stipend, paid in three instalments.
  • Payment can be made directly to the fellow or to their employing organization as a buyout.

5.4 Additional Support

  • £1,000 to support fellowship activities (travel, catering, event expenses).
  • Potential access to additional funds for attending key Digital Humanities events, subject to approval.

Section 6: Application Process

6.1 Required Materials

Applicants must submit the following:

  1. Application Form (including contact details for a reference).
  2. Curriculum Vitae (maximum 2 pages).
  3. Proposal (maximum 1,000 words) outlining interest, research area, and intended outputs.
  4. Implementation Plan (maximum 500 words), optionally supplemented by a Gantt chart.
  5. Letter of Support (if applicable).
  6. Equality and Diversity Form (optional).

6.2 Submission

  • All materials must be submitted as PDFs to: uk-ie.digitalhumanities@sas.ac.uk.

6.3 Deadlines

  • Application deadline: Monday, 17 August 2026 at 23:59 BST.
  • Shortlisting: Week commencing 31 August 2026.
  • Interviews: Week commencing 7 September 2026.
  • Fellowship start: Early October 2026.

Section 7: Key Dates and Timeline

  • Application Deadline: 17 August 2026.
  • Shortlisting: 31 August 2026.
  • Interviews: 7 September 2026.
  • Commencement: October 2026.

Send your application to uk-ie.digitalhumanities@sas.ac.uk today!

Section 8: Potential Research Areas and Projects

Examples of potential projects include:

  • Developing best practice guidance for cross-sector partnerships.
  • Contextualizing differences in research practices between Ireland and the UK.
  • Improving public and open access to digital scholarship.
  • Creating value propositions for Digital Humanities in policy contexts.

Section 9: Benefits of Participation

  • Opportunity to shape advocacy strategies in Digital Humanities.
  • Engagement with leading stakeholders across the UK and Ireland.
  • Professional recognition and financial support.
  • Contribution to a theme of openness and transparency that will influence the field for years to come.

Section 10: Broader Impact on Digital Humanities

The fellowship is expected to have a lasting impact by:

  • Strengthening advocacy for Digital Humanities.
  • Promoting openness and transparency as core values.
  • Enhancing collaboration across sectors.
  • Supporting diversity and inclusion in the field.

Section 11: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

11.1 General Questions

  1. What is the purpose of the fellowship? To advance advocacy in Digital Humanities, focusing on openness and transparency.
  2. Who can apply? Residents of the UK or Ireland with relevant experience in research, digital practice, technical work, or GLAM sectors.
  3. Is joint application allowed? Yes, two individuals may apply together.
  4. What is the time commitment? Approximately 10 hours per month.
  5. What is the stipend? £4,000, plus £1,000 for fellowship activities.

11.2 Application Questions

  1. What documents are required? Application form, CV, proposal, implementation plan, letter of support (if applicable), and optional equality and diversity form.
  2. How should applications be submitted? As PDFs to uk-ie.digitalhumanities@sas.ac.uk.
  3. What is the deadline? 17 August 2026 at 23:59 BST.
  4. When will interviews take place? Week commencing 7 September 2026.
  5. When does the fellowship start? Early October 2026.

11.3 Fellowship Activities

  1. What kind of research will the fellow undertake? Desk research, surveys, stakeholder engagement, and workshops.
  2. What outputs are expected? Reports, podcasts, videos, or other media, shared openly with the community.
  3. Will the fellow attend events? Yes, including regional meetings and potentially other key Digital Humanities events.
  4. Is flexibility allowed in scheduling? Yes, adjustments can be made to start and completion dates.
  5. Can students apply? Yes, with a letter of support from their supervisor.
To learn more about the Digital Humanities Fellowship 2026/27, click HERE.

Conclusion

The 2026/27 Advocacy & Engagement Fellowship represents a unique opportunity to contribute to the advancement of Digital Humanities in the UK and Ireland. By focusing on the theme of Openness and Transparency, the fellowship underscores the Association’s commitment to inclusivity, accountability, and accessibility. The appointed fellow will not only undertake research and stakeholder engagement but also produce outputs that will shape advocacy strategies for years to come. With financial support, flexibility, and a clear mandate, the fellowship offers an invaluable platform for individuals passionate about Digital Humanities to make a lasting impact.

To explore and learn more about other fellowship opportunities, visit the OFY website HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Health policy decisions influence the quality of healthcare systems, determine access to essential medical services, and shape the health outcomes of millions of people. For experienced professionals seeking to move beyond research, clinical practice, or public service into the heart of policymaking, the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) Health Policy Fellows Program provides one of the most prestigious opportunities available.

The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program is a highly respected, nonpartisan leadership fellowship designed specifically for accomplished mid-career professionals who wish to gain firsthand experience in the U.S. federal policymaking process. Through an immersive year-long placement in Washington, DC, fellows work directly alongside members of Congress, congressional committees, or executive branch agencies while contributing to policies that improve health and healthcare across the United States.

Since its establishment in 1973, the fellowship has prepared more than 300 influential leaders who have gone on to shape health policy, strengthen healthcare systems, and influence national conversations on public health and healthcare reform.

This fellowship offers an exceptional combination of policy education, leadership development, practical government experience, strategic communications training, and access to an influential network of policymakers and health leaders.

About the RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program

The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program provides experienced professionals with an extraordinary opportunity to bridge the gap between technical expertise and policymaking.

Participants spend one full year immersed in the federal policy environment, learning how legislation is developed, how executive agencies shape national health priorities, and how evidence is translated into public policy.

Rather than remaining observers, fellows become active participants in federal decision-making.

During the fellowship, participants gain practical experience by contributing directly to the work of policymakers and government officials responsible for shaping America’s health system.

The program equips fellows with:

  • Advanced leadership skills
  • Practical policymaking experience
  • Legislative knowledge
  • Executive branch exposure
  • Strategic communication abilities
  • High-level networking opportunities
  • Long-term professional connections

The fellowship is administered in collaboration with the National Academy of Medicine (NAM), ensuring participants receive world-class policy education and mentorship.

Why This Fellowship Matters

Many experienced professionals possess deep technical expertise but have limited exposure to how federal policies are actually created.

The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program closes that gap by allowing fellows to experience policymaking from the inside.

Participants develop a comprehensive understanding of:

  • Federal legislative processes
  • Executive branch policymaking
  • Congressional operations
  • Health policy development
  • Budget negotiations
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • National healthcare priorities

This experience enables graduates to become stronger leaders capable of influencing healthcare systems at institutional, state, and national levels.

Fellowship Structure

The fellowship is divided into several major phases designed to maximize both learning and practical experience.

Phase 1: Intensive Orientation

The fellowship officially begins in September with an intensive three-and-a-half-month orientation organized by the National Academy of Medicine.

During this period, fellows receive comprehensive preparation before entering government placements.

The orientation includes meetings with:

  • National health leaders
  • Members of Congress
  • Congressional staff
  • Executive branch officials
  • Think tanks
  • Advocacy organizations
  • Policy experts
  • Interest groups

Participants also attend seminars covering topics such as:

  • Health economics
  • Federal healthcare financing
  • Congressional budget processes
  • Current health policy priorities
  • Federal legislative procedures
  • Executive decision-making
  • Health policy analysis

This orientation prepares fellows to contribute immediately once they begin their placements.

Phase 2: Federal Government Placement

Most fellowship placements begin in January.

Each fellow joins either:

  • A congressional office
  • A congressional committee
  • An executive branch agency

Rather than serving as observers, fellows become full members of policy teams under the mentorship of experienced senior staff members.

Throughout the placement, fellows actively contribute to policy development and legislative activities.

Typical responsibilities include:

Policy Development

Fellows help:

  • Develop policy proposals
  • Analyze health legislation
  • Recommend policy positions
  • Conduct policy research

Legislative Drafting

Participants assist in:

  • Drafting legislation
  • Preparing policy amendments
  • Writing legislative summaries

Policy Communications

Fellows prepare:

  • Briefing documents
  • Policy memos
  • Background papers
  • Research summaries

Congressional Engagement

Participants organize:

  • Congressional hearings
  • Stakeholder briefings
  • Policy discussions
  • Committee meetings

Stakeholder Relations

Fellows engage with:

  • Constituents
  • Advocacy organizations
  • Healthcare providers
  • Government agencies
  • Professional associations

Senior Briefings

Participants frequently brief:

  • Members of Congress
  • Congressional staff
  • Executive officials
  • Senior policymakers

This direct exposure allows fellows to understand how national health policies move from concept to implementation.

Additional Leadership Development

The learning experience extends well beyond the workplace.

Throughout the fellowship year, participants continue attending nonpartisan seminars covering emerging health policy issues.

Additional professional development opportunities include:

  • Leadership workshops
  • Strategic communications training
  • Media engagement training
  • Group policy discussions
  • Professional networking events
  • National Academy of Medicine meetings

Each fellow also prepares a formal presentation addressing a health policy issue encountered during the fellowship.

These presentations strengthen analytical, communication, and leadership skills.

Fellowship Extension Opportunity

Although the standard fellowship lasts from September 1 through August 31, fellows may request approval from the National Program Office to remain in Washington beyond the official residential period.

Approved extensions may continue:

  • Through the legislative session
  • Until December 31

This provides additional opportunities for policy engagement and project completion.

Alumni Network

Completion of the fellowship marks the beginning—not the end—of long-term engagement.

Graduates become members of a nationwide alumni community consisting of distinguished health leaders.

Many alumni return annually to Washington, DC, for:

  • Alumni retreats
  • Health policy briefings
  • Professional networking
  • Leadership discussions

The alumni network provides continued opportunities for collaboration throughout participants’ careers.

Eligibility Requirements

The fellowship seeks exceptional professionals with substantial expertise and demonstrated leadership potential.

Applicants must satisfy several eligibility requirements.

Professional Background

Applicants should currently work within:

  • Academic institutions
  • Non-profit organizations
  • Government agencies
  • Military services
  • U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
  • U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps
  • Eligible state government offices

Federal, tribal, state, and local government employees may apply provided they are not classified as government officials under Section 4946 of the Internal Revenue Code.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must possess:

  • A master’s degree; or
  • A doctoral degree

Advanced degrees should relate to a health-related discipline or an area contributing to health policy.

Professional Expertise

Applicants must possess significant expertise in a health-related field.

Examples include:

  • Medicine
  • Nursing
  • Public health
  • Law
  • Dentistry
  • Economics
  • Social sciences
  • Housing policy
  • Transportation
  • Nutrition
  • Wealth and economic policy
  • Employment
  • Education
  • Environmental health
  • Community development
  • Health services research
  • Social work
  • Behavioral health
  • Other health professions

Professionals whose work addresses broader determinants of health are also encouraged to apply.

Ineligible Applicants

The following individuals are not eligible:

  • Professionals whose primary responsibilities involve government relations
  • Individuals whose primary work focuses on advocacy
  • Applicants related by blood or marriage to officers or trustees of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation
  • Descendants of Robert Wood Johnson

Citizenship Requirement

Applicants must be either:

  • U.S. citizens; or
  • U.S. permanent residents

Eligibility is determined at the time of application.

Because fellows work within the federal government, future policy or legal changes could affect fellowship eligibility or placement conditions.

Selection Process

The fellowship uses a rigorous, competitive selection process.

Initial Application Review

Applications are evaluated by the advisory board using several leadership and professional criteria.

Finalist Selection

By mid-January, finalists are selected and invited for interviews.

Interviews

Finalists participate in in-person interviews in Washington, DC during March.

Interview invitations include additional information regarding the remainder of the selection process.

Selection Criteria

Applicants are assessed based on several important qualities.

These include:

  • Outstanding professional accomplishments
  • Leadership potential in health policy
  • Career growth potential
  • Ability to improve health outcomes nationally
  • Communication skills
  • Interpersonal effectiveness
  • Vision for applying fellowship experience to future career goals

Characteristics of Successful Candidates

The fellowship seeks individuals who have already demonstrated excellence within their profession.

Ideal candidates typically:

  • Are recognized leaders in their field
  • Demonstrate professional credibility
  • Show commitment to improving health systems
  • Think strategically
  • Adapt quickly to changing environments
  • Collaborate effectively
  • Learn rapidly
  • Exhibit emotional intelligence
  • Build strong professional relationships
  • Communicate clearly
  • Exercise discretion
  • Display patience and humility
  • Approach challenges with curiosity and critical thinking

The program also strongly encourages applicants from professional disciplines that have historically been underrepresented within the fellowship to apply.

Diverse professional experiences, perspectives, and career pathways are viewed as strengths.

Benefits of the RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program

Participants receive numerous professional and leadership benefits, including:

  • Immersive federal government policy experience
  • Hands-on legislative and executive branch work
  • Intensive policy education
  • Leadership development
  • Strategic communications training
  • Mentorship from experienced policymakers
  • National Academy of Medicine engagement
  • Access to influential national health leaders
  • Long-term alumni network
  • Enhanced leadership credibility
  • Expanded professional network
  • Practical experience influencing national health policy

Why You Should Apply

If you are an accomplished health professional who wants to influence healthcare beyond clinical practice, research, or administration, this fellowship offers a rare opportunity to participate directly in national policymaking.

Graduates leave with practical legislative experience, stronger leadership skills, broader professional networks, and a deeper understanding of how federal decisions shape healthcare across the nation. The experience prepares fellows to become influential leaders capable of advancing meaningful and lasting improvements in health policy.

APPLY HERE

Deadline

At the time of the provided information, no application deadline has been specified. Interested applicants should monitor the official fellowship webpage for application opening and closing dates.

Visit HERE to learn more about the RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program.

Conclusion

The RWJF Health Policy Fellows Program stands among the most prestigious leadership fellowships available for experienced health professionals in the United States. Through an intensive orientation, hands-on placements in Congress or the executive branch, leadership development, policy training, and lifelong alumni engagement, the program equips fellows with the knowledge, experience, and networks needed to influence health policy at the highest levels. For mid-career professionals committed to improving health outcomes and shaping the future of healthcare, this fellowship provides an unparalleled platform to turn expertise into lasting national impact.

For more fellowship opportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is inviting experienced professionals from around the world to join its Consultant Roster, a global talent pool of experts who may be engaged for future consultancy assignments across a wide range of development sectors. This is an excellent opportunity for highly qualified professionals with specialized expertise to contribute to international development, humanitarian action, population issues, gender equality, reproductive health, and sustainable development initiatives. Unlike a traditional job vacancy, the UNFPA Consultant Roster serves as a database of qualified experts who can be contacted when consultancy opportunities arise. Individuals who successfully join the roster may be considered for assignments that match their skills, qualifications, and areas of expertise.

Applicants are strongly advised to carefully complete every section of the application, particularly the “Expertises” section, as this information is essential for matching consultants with future assignments.

Important Notice for Applicants

Applicants must submit their areas of expertise under the “Expertises” section of the application form.

Failure to clearly indicate your professional areas of expertise may reduce your chances of being matched with suitable consultancy assignments.

About the UNFPA Consultant Roster

The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) works to improve reproductive health, promote gender equality, protect human rights, strengthen population data systems, and support sustainable development across more than 150 countries and territories.

To meet its operational needs worldwide, UNFPA maintains a Consultant Roster consisting of highly qualified professionals from diverse backgrounds. Consultants are selected from this roster whenever specific technical expertise is required for projects, programmes, research, policy development, evaluations, training, capacity building, humanitarian response, and other specialized assignments.

Being included in the roster does not guarantee immediate employment or a consultancy contract. Instead, it increases your visibility for future consultancy opportunities that align with your qualifications and experience.

Main Tasks and Responsibilities

Since this is a general consultant roster rather than a vacancy for one specific consultancy, there are no predefined duties.

Instead:

  • Individual consultancy assignments will have their own Terms of Reference (TOR).
  • The responsibilities will vary depending on the nature of each assignment.
  • Consultants may work in different thematic and technical areas based on their expertise.
  • Specific deliverables, timelines, reporting requirements, and expected outputs will be clearly outlined when a consultancy assignment becomes available.

Every consultancy opportunity will define:

  • Scope of work
  • Expected deliverables
  • Duration of assignment
  • Duty station (if applicable)
  • Remote or on-site requirements
  • Required technical expertise
  • Reporting relationships

Qualifications and Experience

The qualifications required depend on the consultancy assignment. However, UNFPA generally seeks professionals who possess:

Educational Qualifications

Applicants are generally expected to have:

  • An advanced university degree in a relevant field.

Fields of study may vary depending on the consultancy assignment and technical area.

Professional Experience

Successful consultants typically possess:

  • Significant professional experience in one or more thematic areas relevant to UNFPA’s work.
  • Demonstrated technical expertise within their field.
  • Experience working with international organizations, governments, research institutions, NGOs, or development partners.
  • Previous consultancy experience, particularly with international development agencies, is considered highly desirable.

Language Requirements

Language requirements may differ depending on each consultancy assignment.

Generally:

  • Fluency in English is required.
  • Knowledge of another United Nations official language may be required or considered an advantage depending on the assignment.

Required Competencies

UNFPA places strong emphasis on recruiting professionals who embody its organizational values and competencies.

Value-Based Competencies

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Exemplifying integrity
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the United Nations system
  • Embracing cultural diversity
  • Embracing change

These values are central to the organization’s mission and guide the conduct of all consultants working with UNFPA.

Core Competencies

Consultants are also expected to demonstrate the ability to:

  • Achieve results effectively
  • Be accountable for assigned responsibilities
  • Apply professional expertise and strong business acumen
  • Think analytically and strategically
  • Collaborate effectively within diverse teams
  • Build and maintain productive professional relationships
  • Communicate clearly and effectively for maximum impact

Additional functional competencies may be specified depending on the technical requirements of a particular consultancy assignment.

UNFPA Work Environment

UNFPA is committed to creating an inclusive, respectful, and supportive work environment.

The organization promotes:

  • Gender equality
  • Diversity and inclusion
  • Respect for different cultures
  • Integrity and professionalism
  • Teamwork and collaboration
  • Work-life balance

UNFPA also strives to maintain balanced gender representation within its workforce and strongly encourages women to apply.

Professionals joining the consultant roster may have opportunities to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across regions while contributing to meaningful global development initiatives.

Compensation and Benefits

UNFPA offers competitive remuneration packages for consultants.

Compensation is determined based on:

  • The complexity of the consultancy assignment
  • Level of expertise required
  • Duration of the consultancy
  • Nature of the assignment

Benefits and payment arrangements will be specified in the Terms of Reference for each consultancy opportunity.

To APPLY click HERE

Why Join the UNFPA Consultant Roster?

Joining the UNFPA Consultant Roster provides several advantages, including:

  • Opportunity to contribute to global development initiatives.
  • Access to future consultancy assignments with the United Nations Population Fund.
  • Opportunities to work on international projects.
  • Engagement with multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
  • Professional recognition as part of a global consultant database.
  • Competitive consultancy remuneration.
  • Potential assignments across multiple countries and regions.
  • Opportunities to support initiatives related to reproductive health, gender equality, population data, humanitarian response, and sustainable development.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Application Tips

To maximize your chances of being selected for future consultancy assignments:

  1. Carefully complete every section of the application.
  2. Clearly list all your areas of expertise in the “Expertises” section.
  3. Highlight your advanced education and relevant professional experience.
  4. Include previous consultancy work, especially with international development organizations.
  5. Demonstrate your language proficiency.
  6. Showcase achievements that align with UNFPA’s core values and competencies.
  7. Ensure your application accurately reflects your technical specialization.

Deadline

No application deadline has been specified in the provided announcement. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible if the consultant roster remains open.

Conclusion

The UNFPA Consultant Roster offers experienced professionals a valuable opportunity to become part of a global network of experts supporting one of the United Nations’ leading development agencies. Although inclusion in the roster does not guarantee an immediate consultancy assignment, it positions qualified candidates for future opportunities aligned with their expertise. Professionals with advanced academic qualifications, substantial international experience, and a commitment to UN values are encouraged to apply and ensure they accurately complete the “Expertises” section of the application to enhance their visibility for future assignments.

For more GLOBAL JOBS click HERE
