item.content:encoded:
The Fellowship for Emerging Leaders in Public Service (FELPS) 2027 is now accepting applications from outstanding early-career professionals committed to building meaningful careers in public service. Hosted by the New York University (NYU) Changemaker Center, FELPS is a highly respected cross-sector leadership development program designed to help the next generation of public service leaders strengthen their leadership skills, expand their professional networks, and intentionally shape their long-term careers while continuing to work full-time.

Since its establishment in 2005, the Fellowship has supported emerging leaders across government agencies, nonprofit organizations, philanthropic institutions, think tanks, and other public service organizations. Rather than requiring participants to leave their jobs, FELPS allows Fellows to continue serving their communities while engaging in a structured leadership development journey that combines expert instruction, career coaching, mentorship, networking, and reflective learning.

Applications for the 2027 cohort are currently open, and all completed applications, including supervisor recommendations, must be submitted by 12:00 PM EST on September 24, 2026.

What is the Fellowship for Emerging Leaders in Public Service (FELPS)?

The Fellowship for Emerging Leaders in Public Service (FELPS) is a premier leadership development initiative offered through the NYU Changemaker Center.

The fellowship recognizes young professionals who have already demonstrated a strong commitment to serving the public and provides them with the tools, relationships, and experiences necessary to become more effective leaders throughout their careers.

Unlike academic degree programs, FELPS focuses entirely on professional growth, helping Fellows think strategically about leadership, career development, and long-term public impact.

Importantly, the fellowship:

  • Is not limited to NYU graduates
  • Is not open exclusively to NYU students
  • Welcomes qualified professionals regardless of where they completed their education
  • Is specifically designed for individuals already working full-time in public service in the New York City area.

Learn More

History of the FELPS Program

The Fellowship was founded in 2005 as a program of NYU’s Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service.

Today, it operates under the NYU Changemaker Center as part of the university’s broader commitment to strengthening leadership within New York City’s public service community.

Over nearly two decades, FELPS has developed a strong reputation for helping early-career professionals clarify their leadership identity while expanding their understanding of the many career paths available in public service.

Purpose of the Fellowship

FELPS is built around a simple but powerful idea:

Great public service leaders require continuous professional development, thoughtful career planning, and meaningful relationships.

The program helps Fellows:

  • Renew their commitment to public service
  • Build intentional career plans
  • Develop leadership skills
  • Expand professional networks
  • Learn from experienced public service leaders
  • Reflect on their professional growth
  • Prepare for long-term leadership roles

Rather than offering technical job training, FELPS focuses on helping participants become more intentional, reflective, and effective leaders.

Program Goals

The fellowship aims to help participants:

  • Strengthen their commitment to public service
  • Explore long-term leadership opportunities
  • Build stronger professional networks
  • Improve career planning skills
  • Gain greater confidence as emerging leaders
  • Learn directly from experienced practitioners
  • Better understand the evolving public service landscape

How FELPS Supports Emerging Leaders

The fellowship is centered around four major pillars.

1. Reconnecting with Purpose

Participants revisit the motivations that inspired them to pursue public service.

Through guided reflection, Fellows:

  • Reexamine personal values
  • Clarify professional goals
  • Renew their commitment to serving communities
  • Identify meaningful future career directions

2. Career Networking

Networking is a central component of the fellowship.

Participants connect with:

  • Senior public service leaders
  • Government officials
  • Nonprofit executives
  • Policy experts
  • Philanthropic leaders
  • Fellow emerging professionals

These relationships often continue long after the fellowship concludes.

3. Dynamic Conversations

FELPS encourages thoughtful discussions about:

  • Leadership
  • Public systems
  • Career choices
  • Professional challenges
  • Ethical decision-making
  • Future opportunities

Participants are continually encouraged to ask:

“What’s next?”

4. Reflective Career Development

The fellowship creates structured opportunities for self-assessment and reflection.

Participants learn how to:

  • Evaluate their strengths
  • Identify growth areas
  • Build intentional career plans
  • Align professional goals with personal values

Fellowship Duration

The 2027 Fellowship runs from:

November 2026 through May 2027.

Approximately 20 Fellows are selected each year to participate in this highly competitive leadership program.

Program Structure

Throughout the fellowship, participants engage in a blend of:

  • Evening workshops
  • Weekend sessions
  • Career exploration activities
  • Networking events
  • Community service activities
  • Small-group discussions
  • Mentorship sessions

Fellows typically meet approximately three times each month through in-person workshops and activities.

What Fellows Will Experience

Participants engage in numerous learning activities throughout the fellowship.

These include:

Learning from Public Service Experts

Senior leaders share insights about:

  • Leadership journeys
  • Career decisions
  • Public service challenges
  • Professional growth
  • Lessons learned

Leadership Self-Assessment

Participants evaluate:

  • Leadership strengths
  • Knowledge base
  • Professional competencies
  • Areas for improvement

Career Planning

Working in small cohort groups, Fellows develop:

  • Five-year career plans
  • Leadership goals
  • Professional development strategies
  • Actionable career roadmaps

Mentorship

Experienced Career Guides provide:

  • Personalized advice
  • Career coaching
  • Professional feedback
  • Leadership insights

Networking

Participants build relationships with:

  • Fellow participants
  • Alumni
  • Mentors
  • Public service leaders
  • Cross-sector professionals

The FELPS Career Development Framework

The fellowship guides participants through four foundational questions.

Why Public Service?

Participants reflect on:

  • Their motivation
  • Career purpose
  • Long-term aspirations
  • Public impact

What’s in My Leadership Toolbox?

Fellows assess:

  • Skills
  • Knowledge
  • Experiences
  • Leadership strengths

Who’s in My Network?

Participants strengthen professional relationships while learning how to leverage networks effectively.

What’s My Career Map?

Through mentorship and career guidance, Fellows gain a deeper understanding of career pathways within public service.

Program Activities

The fellowship includes numerous professional development opportunities, including:

  • Leadership workshops
  • Career coaching
  • Group discussions
  • Networking sessions
  • Reflective exercises
  • Community engagement
  • Mentorship meetings
  • Career planning activities

Learn More

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must satisfy all eligibility requirements.

Educational Requirements

Applicants should:

  • Have graduated from an undergraduate institution within approximately the last 2–4 years
  • Typically possess 2–4 years of full-time professional work experience
  • Not generally have already completed an advanced professional degree, although exceptions may exist depending on individual circumstances.

Employment Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Hold a full-time paid public service position
  • Work in the New York City area
  • Remain employed in public service throughout the fellowship
  • Work in person in or near New York City

Internships and part-time employment do not qualify.

In-Person Participation

Participants must:

  • Be physically located within commuting distance of lower Manhattan
  • Attend all required sessions in person
  • Participate in the mandatory orientation

Remote participation is not permitted.

Visit HERE for more information for applicants.

Public Service Fields Eligible

Professionals working in a wide range of sectors are encouraged to apply, including:

  • Government agencies
  • Nonprofit organizations
  • Philanthropic foundations
  • Offices of elected officials
  • Think tanks
  • Corporate social responsibility programs
  • Public-private partnerships

The fellowship welcomes emerging leaders across the full spectrum of public service.

Selection Criteria

Applicants are evaluated based on:

  • Demonstrated commitment to public service
  • Leadership potential
  • Volunteer and work experience
  • Interest in understanding public systems
  • Willingness to engage in collaborative learning
  • Professional growth potential

Program Expectations

Successful Fellows are expected to:

  • Attend the mandatory orientation
  • Participate in all fellowship sessions
  • Complete weekly assignments
  • Engage actively in discussions
  • Share knowledge with peers
  • Build lasting professional relationships

Assignments typically require two to three additional hours per week outside scheduled sessions.

Program Fee

Although much of the fellowship cost is subsidized by NYU and generous supporters, Fellows are required to contribute a program fee.

For the 2027 cohort:

  • Program Fee: $650
  • Payment Due: October 29, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to seek financial support from their employers.

Unfortunately:

  • Scholarships are not available.
  • Payment plans are not offered.

Application Process

Applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Review Eligibility

Ensure you satisfy all eligibility requirements and can attend all required sessions.

Step 2: Complete the Online Application

Applicants must submit:

  • Online application
  • Resume
  • Short personal statement

Step 3: Supervisor Recommendation

After submitting the application:

  • A recommendation link is sent to the applicant.
  • The applicant’s current direct supervisor must complete the recommendation form.

Recommendations from professors, former supervisors, or colleagues are not accepted.

Click HERE to submit your application!

Important Dates

Applicants should take note of the following timeline:

  • Applications Open: Currently Open
  • Application Deadline: 12:00 PM EST, September 24, 2026
  • Acceptance Notification: October 14, 2026
  • Program Fee Due: October 29, 2026
  • Mandatory Orientation: November 7, 2026 (9:00 AM–3:00 PM EST)
  • Program Duration: November 2026 – May 2027

Why You Should Apply

The NYU Fellowship for Emerging Leaders in Public Service offers much more than traditional leadership training.

Participants gain:

  • Leadership development
  • Career coaching
  • Professional mentoring
  • Cross-sector networking
  • Career planning support
  • Exposure to experienced public service leaders
  • A lifelong professional network
  • Practical leadership skills that can accelerate careers in public service

For professionals committed to making a lasting impact in government, nonprofit organizations, philanthropy, and related sectors, FELPS provides an outstanding platform for long-term leadership growth.

Click HERE to learn more about the NYU Fellowship for Emerging Leaders in Public Service (FELPS) 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

FELPS is looking for early career professionals who have the following characteristics:

  • Commitment to public service. The ideal candidate will possess a work record, including summer, campus and/or volunteer experience in public service. In addition to their prior public service work, the ideal candidate will be able to convey a clear vision for a long-term engagement with public service.
  • Commitment to discussing the systems that operate in the public service space.
  • Willingness to authentically engage with other members of the fellowship in conversations.
  • Capacity for leadership. The ideal candidate will have exercised leadership on some public service activity on campus and/or in their community and be recognized by their employer as having the potential for continued leadership.
  • Position in public service. Participants should have a full-time public service position in the New York metropolitan area that allows them to appreciate the breadth of opportunities within public service.

The program is heavily subsidized by generous gifts. In typical years the cost to each participant was $800. For the 2027 Fellowship year, this cost is reduced to $650.

We suggest that each fellow encourage their organization to fund their participation in this valuable professional development opportunity, but that is up to the discretion of the individual and organization; each fellow is ultimately responsible for the $650 payment. You can pay via credit card or check, and all necessary payment information will be included as part of the acceptance packet. Payment must be received in full by the October 29, 2026 deadline for Fellows to participate in the program.

Unfortunately, we are not able to offer scholarships or payment plans. We do encourage Fellows to see if their organizations are willing to contribute some or all of the cost as an investment in their professional development.

Generous gifts subsidize the bulk of the program cost for each Fellowship.

You must be working full-time in a paid public service position in the New York City area to apply for FELPS and must remain in a public service position throughout the fellowship. Unfortunately, internships and part-time work (including multiple part-time jobs) do not qualify.

Not unless you are certain you will be physically living and working in the NYC area beginning in November. If you are unable to join in-person sessions you will not be able to participate in the fellowship.

Regardless of additional educational experiences, applicants should have graduated from their undergraduate institutions within the last 2 to 4 years. The fellowship is designed for emerging leaders who have not yet solidified their career interests with a professional degree and employment in a specific field — for the most part, this means they will not have already pursued an advanced degree (Masters, PhD, JD, etc.). Many of our fellows choose to continue their education by enrolling in professional programs within a few years of completing the fellowship.

We strongly encourage anyone in a public service position to apply. This includes people working for nonprofit organizations, government agencies, offices of elected officials, philanthropic foundations and programs, think tanks, and private corporations focused on public service work (such as corporate social responsibility programs or in partnership programs with government).

In the past, Fellows have come from a range of backgrounds and interests. The program provides tools for successful leaders in any field of public service work. Sessions are not field-specific and are intended for emerging leaders across the full spectrum of public service.

Instead of writing a formal letter of recommendation, your current direct supervisor will complete a brief online recommendation form. Recommendations from professors, previous supervisors or someone in a role other than that of your direct supervisor are not accepted. We understand that you may be new to a position and we take that into consideration when reviewing your recommendation.

We look for examples of commitment and enthusiasm in your work, as well as your supervisor’s recognition that you will be involved in a robust fellowship program that will require their commitment to ensure that you can attend all sessions on time and participate fully.

Unfortunately, no. The November Orientation is mandatory for all Fellows. No exceptions will be made for any reason. If you cannot attend the Orientation this year, or any of our other sessions as listed on the calendar, we encourage you to apply next year. Fellows who miss more than one regular session after orientation may be dismissed from the program.

Fellows are expected to:

  • Attend all events including a mandatory Orientation on November 7, 2026, sessions approximately three times a month and a final reception. Fellows must be able to begin evening sessions promptly at 6 pm. Fellows should be able to arrive at evening session locations in Manhattan (usually at NYU’s Washington Square campus) by 5:50 pm.
  • Meet all deadlines and complete all assignments (which will require approximately two to three additional hours beyond the sessions each week).
  • Share thoughts, experiences, and contacts with other Fellows and alumni.
  • Participants and employers will be asked to sign a statement of commitment at the beginning of the program for the full duration of the fellowship, which runs from November 2026 through May 2027.

If you have reviewed the Web site and still have a question, please email Mo Coffey, FELPS Director, at mcoffey@nyu.edu

You can expect an answer to your email in three business days, but usually sooner.

Email is the best, only, and fastest way to have your questions answered. We are unable to accept phone inquiries.

Conclusion

The NYU Fellowship for Emerging Leaders in Public Service (FELPS) 2027 is an exceptional opportunity for early-career public service professionals seeking to strengthen their leadership capacity while continuing to serve their communities. Through a seven-month blend of workshops, mentorship, career planning, networking, and reflective learning, Fellows gain the skills, relationships, and confidence needed to navigate complex public service careers and create meaningful impact.

Hosted by the NYU Changemaker Center, the program equips participants to reconnect with their purpose, expand their professional networks, and develop intentional career strategies that will shape their future as leaders in public service. With a highly competitive cohort of approximately 20 Fellows each year, applicants are encouraged to prepare their application materials early, secure their supervisor’s recommendation, and submit all required documents before the 12:00 PM EST deadline on September 24, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The United States International University-Africa (USIU-Africa), through its WATERSHED Research Project, has opened applications for a fully funded PhD in International Relations, offering an outstanding opportunity for aspiring researchers interested in climate adaptation, urban resilience, gender studies, and climate justice.

Hosted by the Department of International Relations at USIU-Africa in Nairobi, Kenya, this doctoral opportunity is designed for highly motivated graduates who wish to contribute to groundbreaking research addressing climate change and flooding challenges affecting informal urban settlements.

Funded by the Danida Fellowship Centre (DFC), the WATERSHED Project seeks to bridge the gap between community-led climate adaptation initiatives and formal climate governance, producing research that informs policy while amplifying the voices of vulnerable communities.

Application Deadline

Deadline: 17 August 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be considered, so interested applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications well before the deadline.

About USIU-Africa

United States International University-Africa (USIU-Africa) is one of East Africa’s leading private universities, recognized for delivering globally competitive education and research.

The university’s School of Humanities and Social Sciences promotes excellence in teaching, research, and innovation while preparing graduates to become critical thinkers and global citizens capable of addressing complex regional and international challenges.

The fully funded doctoral opportunity is offered through the Department of International Relations, providing scholars with an environment that supports interdisciplinary research and international collaboration.

About the WATERSHED Research Project

The PhD position forms part of the WATERSHED Project, a research initiative funded by the Danida Fellowship Centre (DFC).

The project focuses on understanding how informal communities respond to increasing climate risks, particularly flooding, in Nairobi’s rapidly growing urban settlements.

Rather than examining climate adaptation only from the perspective of governments and institutions, WATERSHED investigates the everyday actions taken by community members and local activists who often play a critical role in building resilience despite receiving limited recognition.

The project explores how grassroots initiatives can contribute to broader climate governance and policy development while addressing the challenges created by urbanization, environmental degradation, and changing development funding priorities.

Read More

Research Focus of the PhD Project

The selected PhD researcher will develop a research project centered on:

  • Flooding in Nairobi’s informal settlements
  • Community responses to climate change
  • Gendered dimensions of climate adaptation
  • Climate justice
  • Informal governance
  • Urban resilience
  • Community-led adaptation strategies

The research will specifically examine flooding and community and gender-related activities associated with climate adaptation measures in informal settlements across Nairobi.

Areas of Study

Applicants may draw on perspectives from several disciplines, including:

  • International Relations
  • Political Science
  • Sociology
  • Gender Studies
  • Human Geography
  • Anthropology
  • Development Studies
  • Other related Social Science fields

This interdisciplinary approach allows the researcher to investigate climate adaptation from political, social, economic, environmental, and cultural perspectives.

Why This Research Matters

Climate change continues to increase the frequency and severity of flooding across many urban areas in Africa.

Informal settlements are often among the hardest-hit communities because they typically experience:

  • Poor drainage infrastructure
  • High population density
  • Limited public services
  • Inadequate housing
  • Greater exposure to environmental hazards

Despite these challenges, local communities

The WATERSHED Project seeks to document and understand these efforts while identifying how community knowledge can inform future climate policies and decision-making.

Key Research Themes

The project examines several interconnected themes, including:

1. Climate Adaptation

Understanding how communities adapt to recurring flooding and changing environmental conditions.

2. Climate Justice

Investigating whether vulnerable populations receive equitable support and representation in climate decision-making.

3. Community Activism

Exploring how local residents organize themselves to improve resilience and advocate for better environmental management.

4. Urban Governance

Assessing the relationship between government policies, planning decisions, and climate vulnerability.

5. Gender and Climate Change

Examining how flooding and climate adaptation affect different groups within communities, particularly women and other marginalized populations.

Study Locations

The research will focus on three densely populated informal settlements located along Nairobi’s river systems:

  • Mathare
  • Pumwani
  • Korogocho

These communities provide important case studies for understanding climate vulnerability and local adaptation practices within rapidly expanding urban environments.

Project Objectives

The WATERSHED Project aims to:

  • Understand local perceptions of climate vulnerability.
  • Examine community-led climate adaptation initiatives.
  • Investigate climate justice actions within informal settlements.
  • Explore the relationship between grassroots adaptation and formal climate governance.
  • Generate evidence that can improve future climate policies.
  • Strengthen knowledge on urban resilience in rapidly growing African cities.

Who Should Apply?

The university encourages applications from qualified and motivated candidates with a passion for research and social impact.

Applicants should possess a graduate degree in one of the following disciplines:

  • Political Science
  • International Relations
  • Sociology
  • Gender Studies
  • Human Geography
  • Anthropology
  • Development Studies
  • Other relevant Social Science disciplines

Candidates with research interests aligned with climate change, governance, urban development, community engagement, or environmental justice are particularly encouraged to apply.

Funding

This is a fully funded PhD position under the WATERSHED Research Project, supported by the Danida Fellowship Centre (DFC).

The announcement confirms that the PhD position is fully funded. However, it does not specify the exact financial package or benefits. Applicants are encouraged to consult the official call document or contact the project team for additional funding details.

Why You Should Apply

This opportunity offers numerous advantages, including:

  • Full funding for doctoral studies.
  • Opportunity to conduct impactful research on climate change and urban resilience.
  • Collaboration with experienced researchers and academic experts.
  • Participation in an internationally funded research initiative.
  • Contribution to evidence-based climate governance and policy development.
  • Research experience addressing real-world environmental and social challenges.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should submit their application in accordance with the official PhD call issued by USIU-Africa.

Applicants should ensure that:

  1. They meet the eligibility requirements.
  2. Their research interests align with the WATERSHED Project.
  3. All required application materials are submitted before the deadline.
  4. Their application is complete, as incomplete submissions will not be considered.

APPLY NOW

Contact Information

For inquiries regarding the PhD position, applicants may contact:

Email 1: nwamai@usiu.ac.ke

Email 2: watershedscholar@usiu.ac.ke

Applicants are also encouraged to consult the official Call for PhD Researcher – WATERSHED Project for detailed application requirements and submission instructions.

Conclusion

The Fully Funded PhD in International Relations under the WATERSHED Project at USIU-Africa presents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring researchers who want to contribute to meaningful solutions for climate adaptation, climate justice, and urban resilience in Africa. By examining community-led responses to flooding in Nairobi’s informal settlements, the successful candidate will be part of an internationally funded research initiative with the potential to influence policy, strengthen climate governance, and improve the lives of vulnerable urban communities. Prospective applicants with backgrounds in the social sciences and a commitment to impactful research should take advantage of this opportunity and ensure they submit a complete application before 17 August 2026.

Visit the OFY website for more Fellowship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The Green Africa Youth Organization is inviting applications for the Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026, a two-day capacity-building programme designed to equip young entrepreneurs and waste workers with the practical knowledge, business skills, and professional networks needed to establish, formalize, and scale sustainable businesses.

Formerly known as the Youth Ecopreneurs Summit and Training, the programme has evolved into a comprehensive training initiative that supports youth-led green enterprises while promoting environmental sustainability and economic empowerment.

The training is specifically designed for residents of Accra, Ghana, and provides participants with expert-led sessions, practical workshops, mentorship opportunities, and networking experiences that can help transform innovative green business ideas into successful enterprises.

Application Deadline: 14 August 2026

About the Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026

The Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers is a strategic initiative focused on empowering young entrepreneurs working within the green economy. As environmental sustainability continues to become an important part of economic development, there is an increasing demand for businesses that provide innovative and environmentally responsible solutions.

This programme seeks to bridge the knowledge gap by equipping participants with the entrepreneurial, financial, and marketing skills required to build sustainable businesses that contribute positively to both society and the environment.

Whether participants already operate a small green business or are still developing an innovative business concept, the training provides practical guidance to help them move to the next stage of business development.

The programme combines classroom learning with practical workshops, allowing participants to gain real-world insights into running successful green enterprises.

Objectives of the Programme

The Green Business Training aims to prepare participants for long-term success by helping them:

  • Understand the fundamentals of business structuring and business management.
  • Improve financial literacy and develop sound financial management practices.
  • Learn about available investment opportunities for green businesses.
  • Build effective branding and digital marketing strategies.
  • Connect with experienced entrepreneurs and professionals within the green economy.
  • Learn practical approaches to attracting funding and investment.
  • Develop strategies for formalizing and scaling environmentally sustainable businesses.

What Participants Will Learn

The training covers a broad range of topics that are essential for launching, managing, and expanding a successful green enterprise.

1. Business Structuring and Business Management

Participants will receive practical guidance on how to establish and organize their businesses for sustainable growth.

Topics include:

  • Business planning
  • Business registration and formalization
  • Organizational management
  • Operational planning
  • Strategic decision-making
  • Building sustainable business models

Understanding these areas will help participants build businesses capable of long-term success.

2. Financial Literacy and Investment Readiness

Financial management is one of the most important components of business success.

Participants will gain knowledge on:

  • Financial planning
  • Budgeting
  • Managing business finances
  • Preparing businesses for investors
  • Understanding investment opportunities
  • Improving financial sustainability

The training will also introduce participants to methods for making their businesses more attractive to potential investors and funding organizations.

3. Access to Funding and Grant Writing

One of the major challenges facing young entrepreneurs is securing financial support.

Participants will explore:

  • Available funding opportunities
  • Grant application strategies
  • Proposal writing techniques
  • Preparing funding applications
  • Understanding donor expectations

These sessions are intended to improve participants’ ability to successfully compete for grants and other sources of business financing.

4. Digital Marketing and Branding

In today’s digital economy, having a strong online presence is essential.

Participants will learn how to:

  • Develop a recognizable business brand
  • Market products and services online
  • Improve customer engagement
  • Increase business visibility
  • Build effective digital marketing campaigns

The programme will provide practical strategies that entrepreneurs can apply immediately to grow their businesses.

5. Networking and Mentorship

A successful business often depends on having access to experienced professionals and valuable business networks.

Participants will have opportunities to:

  • Meet fellow young entrepreneurs.
  • Connect with industry experts.
  • Interact with successful green business leaders.
  • Build partnerships within the green entrepreneurship ecosystem.
  • Learn from experienced mentors.

These networking opportunities can lead to future collaborations, partnerships, and business growth.

Benefits of Participating

Successful participants will enjoy several valuable benefits, including:

  • Comprehensive training in green business development.
  • Practical knowledge in business operations and management.
  • Improved financial planning and investment readiness.
  • Training on grant writing and funding opportunities.
  • Digital marketing and branding skills.
  • Opportunities to network with entrepreneurs and industry experts.
  • Professional mentorship.
  • A certificate upon successful completion of the programme.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must satisfy all of the following eligibility requirements:

  • Be a resident of Accra, Ghana.
  • Be between 16 and 35 years old.
  • Have an existing small-scale green business in areas such as:
    • Waste management
    • Sustainable agriculture
    • Renewable energy
    • Eco-friendly manufacturing
    • Other environmentally sustainable sectors
  • Alternatively, applicants may have a well-developed green business idea within the same sectors.
  • Demonstrate commitment to formalizing and expanding their business or business idea.
  • Be available to attend the complete two-day training programme.

Why You Should Apply

The Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers offers more than classroom instruction. It provides participants with practical entrepreneurial skills, exposure to experienced professionals, and access to networks that can support long-term business success.

Young entrepreneurs working in environmental sustainability often face challenges related to funding, business management, and market access. This programme addresses these challenges by providing targeted training designed specifically for businesses operating within the green economy.

Participants will leave the programme with stronger business knowledge, improved financial planning skills, enhanced marketing capabilities, and valuable professional connections that can contribute to the growth of their enterprises.

APPLY NOW

Important Deadline

Applications for the Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026 close on:

14 August 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

Additional Information

  • The programme is strictly for residents of Accra, Ghana.
  • Attendance for the entire two-day training programme is mandatory.
  • Only selected applicants will receive further communication regarding participation.

Conclusion

The Green Business Training for Youth and Waste Workers 2026 presents an excellent opportunity for young entrepreneurs and waste workers in Accra to strengthen their business knowledge, develop practical entrepreneurial skills, and connect with professionals within Ghana’s growing green economy.

Whether you already operate a sustainable business or have an innovative green business idea, this programme offers valuable training in business development, financial management, digital marketing, grant writing, and networking. Participants will also benefit from mentorship opportunities and receive a certificate upon successful completion.

If you meet the eligibility requirements and are committed to building or expanding a green enterprise that contributes to environmental sustainability, be sure to submit your application before the 14 August 2026 deadline.

Visit the OFY website for more Training Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Securing funding often depends on the quality of a grant proposal. However, obtaining meaningful feedback before submitting a proposal can be one of the biggest challenges facing nonprofits, researchers, social enterprises, and community organizations. To address this gap, the Unfunded List Grant Proposal Feedback Program 2026 is inviting organizations and proposal writers to submit their grant applications for expert review and constructive feedback.

Rather than providing funding directly, the Unfunded List helps organizations improve their proposals through a structured review process designed to increase competitiveness and strengthen future funding applications.

The submission deadline for the current round is September 20, 2026.

About the Unfunded List

The Unfunded List is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization committed to demystifying philanthropy through education, collaboration, and feedback.

The organization believes that great ideas deserve both feedback and funding. By connecting applicants with experienced evaluators, the Unfunded List creates opportunities for organizations to refine their proposals, strengthen their fundraising strategies, and improve their chances of securing grants.

How the Feedback Process Works

The Unfunded List follows a structured review process that helps organizations receive thoughtful and actionable feedback.

Step 1: Submit Your Proposal

Organizations submit an existing grant proposal through the Unfunded List application process.

Step 2: Evaluator Assignment

Each proposal is assigned to a cohort of reviewers and evaluators with experience in grant assessment and proposal review.

Step 3: Proposal Review

Evaluators carefully assess the proposal and provide detailed feedback on its strengths, weaknesses, clarity, and competitiveness.

Step 4: Feedback Report

The individual reviews are compiled into a comprehensive report that highlights key recommendations and opportunities for improvement.

Step 5: Feedback Discussion

Participants receive an opportunity to discuss the feedback with the Unfunded List team, helping them better understand how to strengthen future submissions.

Why Participate?

Organizations that participate in the program can benefit from:

• Independent review of grant proposals

• Constructive and actionable feedback

• Insights from experienced evaluators

• Improved proposal quality and competitiveness

• Increased understanding of funder expectations

• Opportunities to strengthen future funding applications

• Access to a collaborative learning community

Who Can Apply?

The program welcomes proposals from a wide range of organizations and applicants.

Eligible participants may include:

• Nonprofit organizations

• Community-based organizations

• Social enterprises

• Researchers

• Educational institutions

• Charitable initiatives

• International organizations

Organizations do not need to be based in the United States to participate.

Applicants who have previously received grant funding are also encouraged to apply.

Program Cost

To ensure active participation and commitment, the Unfunded List charges a modest fee for first-time participants.

First-Time Submission Fee

• $100 per proposal

Future Participation

Organizations that fully engage in the review process and participate as evaluators may be invited to submit future proposals at no additional cost.

Questions regarding participation fees can be directed to:

📧 dave@unfundedlist.com

Benefits of Joining the Learning Community

The Unfunded List emphasizes continuous learning and improvement. Organizations that engage repeatedly in the process often gain the greatest benefit.

Participants are encouraged to:

• Submit proposals in future review rounds

• Join evaluator committees

• Learn from other proposal writers

• Strengthen grant-writing skills over time

• Build long-term fundraising capacity

Important Dates

Proposal Submission Deadline

📅 September 20, 2026

Feedback Delivery

📅 By December 1, 2026

Why Feedback Matters

Many organizations invest significant time and effort into preparing grant proposals, yet they rarely receive detailed explanations when applications are unsuccessful. The Unfunded List helps fill this gap by offering a rare opportunity to receive expert insights before resubmitting or pursuing future funding opportunities.

Whether your proposal is intended for foundations, government grants, research funding, or philanthropic organizations, thoughtful feedback can help identify areas for improvement and increase the likelihood of future success.

Conclusion

The Unfunded List Grant Proposal Feedback Program offers a valuable opportunity for nonprofits, researchers, and mission-driven organizations to strengthen their grant applications through expert review and collaborative learning. If you are preparing a funding proposal and would benefit from constructive feedback before your next submission, this program could help improve both your proposal quality and your long-term fundraising strategy.

Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The African Economic Research Consortium (AERC), in partnership with the World Bank Africa Region Chief Economist’s Office (AFRCE), is inviting applications for the AERC-World Bank Visiting Scholars Program 2026/2027. This prestigious fellowship offers African researchers the opportunity to spend between four and six months at the World Bank, collaborate with leading economists, and strengthen research that contributes to Africa’s development agenda.

The program is a key component of the collaboration between AERC and the World Bank aimed at enhancing economic policy research, strengthening academic networks, and increasing the policy impact of research across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Applications are open until September 6, 2026.

About the AERC-World Bank Visiting Scholars Program

The Visiting Scholars Program was established under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between AERC and the World Bank’s Africa Region Chief Economist’s Office. Through this initiative, selected scholars gain access to the World Bank’s extensive research resources, professional networks, and analytical expertise.

The fellowship is designed to support African researchers working on development-focused economic research while fostering stronger collaboration between African scholars and World Bank researchers.

Program Objectives

The collaboration seeks to:

• Enhance AERC’s capacity to strengthen economic policy research in Sub-Saharan Africa.

• Strengthen global academic and policy linkages for AERC researchers.

• Increase the policy influence and impact of research conducted by both AERC and the World Bank.

• Improve the research output, publication record, and teaching capacity of African researchers through access to World Bank resources, data, and networks.

Fellowship Benefits
